newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ markets react sluggishly to RBNZ warning.
newsitem.headline: NZ markets react sluggishly to RBNZ warning.

text.p: New Zealand financial markets were barely changed from their early levels on Thursday shortly after the central bank said monetary conditions had eased too far, but the dollar appeared to be firming marginally

At 1.15 p.m. (0115 GMT), 15 minutes after the surprise statement, the Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) had risen to 764.81 from its 761.59 open, bringing conditions to 60 basis points softer than the RBNZ's desired level.

The kiwi dollar was quoted at US$0.6775/82 compared with US$0.6774/81 in early morning trade. On its Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi was at 66.47, flat with its 66.47 at the open and up from the 66.28 just before the announcement.

Ninety-day bank bills were equally sluggish in their response. They were at 7.10 percent from 7.03 percent at the open. Volumes were large in the bank bill futures, with the September contract weakening 13 basis points to 92.90 with 6,738 contracts traded. The September contract had opened at 92.96.
"Actual monetary conditions have been too easy over recent days. We will be looking to see actual conditions settle clower to the announced desired levels," RBNZ governor Don Brash said.

The RBNZ in its Monetary Policy Statement on Friday assumed conditions on the MCI would average 825 over the September quarter, but it also said it would be comfortable if conditions moved about 50 basis points on either side of that average.
